clue.text: Assets and liabilities of London with 100% employment?

definitions.meaning: the accounting measure of current assets less current liabilities, the money a business has to run day to day
a whimsical reading: the UK's chief city when every resident has a job

explanation.surface: An economist ponders London's balance sheet if every Londoner had a job.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a playful literal reading: a capital city that is entirely in work.
explanation.definitionFit: An accounting term for the funds available for day-to-day operations, current assets minus current liabilities.

clue.text: Pigment with touch of red in ridge

indicators.note: in puts the first letter of red inside the darts ridge

parts.note: the oche is the line or raised ridge on the floor behind which darts players stand

indicators.note: a touch is a small amount, so only the opening letter of red is taken

explanation.surface: A coloured dye with a hint of red in a mountain crest.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCHE is the throwing line in darts, a popular British pub game.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthy natural pigment ranging from pale yellow to brownish red.

clue.text: More competitive mourner

definitions.meaning: a person who wails for the dead, especially at an Irish funeral

explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning eager; also a professional wailer at a funeral.

clue.text: Announce with a hymn and date — 4th of June, as arranged

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the fourth letter of June is taken

explanation.surface: Wedding plans: a hymn chosen and the date fixed for June 4th.
explanation.walkthrough: '4th of June' looks like a date but gives the E of June.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to fix and declare the date of one's wedding.

clue.text: Is incapacitated? Humbug!

definitions.meaning: is unable, the contraction of cannot

explanation.definitionFit: Read with an apostrophe it means is unable; without, it is hypocritical pious talk.

clue.text: Horse is bipedal unusually

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of bipedal are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A horse is unusually walking on two legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with irregular patches of black and white is described with this word.

clue.text: It may cause an interruption to services

definitions.text: It may cause an interruption to services

parts.words: It may cause an interruption to services
parts.note: services are serves in a racket game; one clipping the barrier in the middle is a let and must be replayed

explanation.surface: Something that might disrupt public utilities or church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'services' suggests trains or church, but means serves in a racket game.
explanation.definitionFit: The mesh barrier across a court; a serve clipping it is replayed.

clue.text: Disappoint the team, when whistle denoted foul

indicators.note: foul means bad or corrupt, so the letters are corrupted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A player fails the side when the referee blows for a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foul' looks like the referee's decision but signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for failing one's colleagues by performing badly.

clue.text: Monsieur Peston serving starter

indicators.note: serving up food suggests the letters are dished out in a new order

explanation.surface: A Frenchman named Peston dishes up the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monsieur Peston' looks like a waiter's name but is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick Italian vegetable broth with pasta, eaten as a first course.

clue.text: Mongoose chewing coati's tail with one munch

indicators.note: an animal's tail is its end, so only the last letter of coati's is taken
chewing mashes things up, so the letters that follow are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mongoose eats a coati, starting with its tail, in a single bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewing' scrambles I (the tail of coati), ONE and MUNCH together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian mongoose is also known by this old name, famed for eating crocodile eggs.

clue.text: German painter formerly without name

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece is wrapped round the second

parts.note: erst is an archaic word for formerly or once

explanation.surface: A German artist was once anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: ERST goes around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born Dada and Surrealist painter.

clue.text: He is one

parts.note: He looks like the pronoun but is the chemical symbol for helium, which is one of the substances in the periodic table

explanation.surface: A man is identified as one of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is not a man but helium, chemical symbol He.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium is a chemical substance made of a single kind of atom, listed in the periodic table.

clue.text: Showy decoration that's not new

indicators.note: that's not new says the decoration is without its N

parts.note: a garnish is a decoration on food

explanation.surface: A flashy ornament that isn't brand new.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something loud and vulgarly bright, gaudy and attention-seeking.

clue.text: Packs waffles full of old wine

indicators.note: full of says one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: havers is Scots for talks nonsense, waffles
sack is an old name for sherry-like white wine

explanation.surface: Bags filled with waffles soaked in vintage wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Packs' and 'waffles' both look like nouns; 'waffles' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags carried on the back by hikers, rucksacks.

clue.text: Country take-away?

definitions.meaning: a West African nation lying between Ghana and Benin
food ordered to be carried out of the restaurant is, in American usage, for consumption off the premises

explanation.definitionFit: A West African republic; also the American phrase for food bought to be eaten elsewhere.

clue.text: Fruit and raw egg — a disaster

parts.note: green means raw or inexperienced

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook's mishap with fruit and raw egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' scrambles EGG and A into GAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet green-skinned variety of plum.

clue.text: Flowers and antelope in these French surroundings

indicators.note: the French word forms the surroundings, enclosing the other pieces

parts.note: ces is the French word for these
the eland is a large African antelope
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wildflowers and an antelope seen in some French landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesser celandines and greater celandines are yellow-flowered plants of hedgerows and woods.

clue.text: Nothing confines walks here

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
to pen is to confine, as with sheep
paces are steps taken when walking

explanation.surface: A place where you can roam freely with no fences.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer while also building it: O, then PENS, then PACES.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbuilt countryside or parkland where people may roam freely without barriers.

clue.text: Abrasive tools for Indian wood

definitions.meaning: power tools that smooth wood with sandpaper
red sandalwood from India, used as a dye

explanation.surface: Woodworking tools for treating Indian timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a smoothing tool; also a name for the red sandalwood tree of India.

clue.text: Is he attractive to half the undergraduates?

definitions.text: Is he attractive to half the undergraduates?

indicators.note: half says the word for undergraduates loses its second four letters

parts.note: undergraduates are university students

explanation.surface: Is this man the heart-throb of the female half of the student body?
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' trims a word for undergraduates to its first four letters; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a sexually attractive, virile young man, from the breeding-stallion sense.

clue.text: An objection even for hydrocarbon

parts.note: but is an objection, as in no buts
e'en, the poetic contraction of even, has the alternative spelling ene

explanation.surface: Someone raises a point against a fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: ENE is a less familiar spelling of the poetic e'en.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-carbon alkene gas, C4H8, a simple hydrocarbon.

clue.text: Warming effect of 1-0 disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruins, so the score's letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a football score of one-nil

explanation.surface: A one-nil defeat as the cause of global warming.
explanation.walkthrough: 1-0 is read as ONE NIL, whose letters are scrambled by 'disaster'.
explanation.definitionFit: The periodic warming of the eastern Pacific Ocean, which disrupts weather worldwide.

clue.text: Sure! Doc ordered and obtained goods

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor agrees and places an order for supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: Ignore the exclamation mark: 'Sure' and 'Doc' are joined as anagram fodder for 'ordered'.
explanation.definitionFit: In business jargon, to get supplies from a particular supplier is to procure them.

clue.text: Hoard of notes and coins, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for money is as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: banknotes and coins are cash

explanation.surface: A stash of banknotes and coins, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden store of valuables or supplies.

clue.text: Drug addict having rifle mother took away

indicators.note: took away says mother is removed from the gun's name

parts.note: the Mauser is a German bolt-action rifle
ma is mother

explanation.surface: An addict with a gun had it confiscated by his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes illegal drugs regularly.

clue.text: Native American round oracle

parts.note: O is round in shape
a sage is a wise person consulted like an oracle

explanation.surface: A tribal elder sits in a circle and gives wise counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American people of the Great Plains, originally from the Ohio valley, later Oklahoma.

clue.text: Conservation area by pub that's above criticism

parts.note: SAC is a Special Area of Conservation, a European wildlife designation
the Red Cow is a common English pub name

explanation.surface: A protected nature reserve next to a pub that no one may fault.
explanation.walkthrough: The Red Cow is a widespread British pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an institution or idea treated as beyond questioning, from Hindu veneration of cattle.

clue.text: Holidaymaker requests river by deer, we're told

parts.note: pleas are earnest requests
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

indicators.note: we're told means the word for deer is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: the sika is a species of deer from East Asia

explanation.surface: A tourist makes demands by a river near some deer.
explanation.walkthrough: Only SIKA is turned into its sound-alike; PLEAS and URE are spelt as given.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on vacation is out for enjoyment and fun, so is a hedonist in search of delight.
